title: doppeldata fault record
description: One fault `malformed_rows` placed, as a line of `_faults.jsonl`.

column.description: The column the fault is in, or null where it breaks the record or the file.

detail.description:
What the fault wrote, under keys its `kind` sets, such as `text` for a `type_invalid`. Empty
for a kind that writes nothing more than its name says, such as `bom`.

file.description:
The object's path under the destination, as the manifest's `files` names it, or its
`cdc.files` for a fault in a change stream. Beside a one-file write, that file's name.

kind.description:
What broke: a kind `malformed_rows` names in `kinds`, or a fault `cdc` places in a change
stream.

line.description:
The 1-based line the broken record starts on, a header counted. Null in a JSON array or a
Parquet file, and for a fault of the whole file.

row.description:
The dataset row the record was generated as, or in a change stream the row of its key, which
lies past `dataset_rows` for a key the stream inserts. Null for a copy `duplicates` wrote,
and for a fault of the whole file.

FaultKind.description: One way a file is broken. A row kind breaks one record, and a file kind a whole file.

oneOf.description: A record ending before its last 1 to n − 1 fields.
A record carrying 1 or 2 fields past the last.
A lone quote inside a quoted field.
A line break inside a quoted string field, which is legal CSV.
`N/A`, `-`, `?` or a unit suffix in place of a typed value, or text of another type.
A lone continuation byte or the bytes C3 28 inside a field.
A record past DuckDB's default `max_line_size`.
The file's last record cut mid-field, with no line break, as a cut-off upload leaves it.
A file starting with the UTF-8 byte order mark.
A file whose records end in LF, CRLF and CR mixed.
A file written with another delimiter than the rest.
A file whose header renames a column or swaps two, its values swapped with it.
A file encoded windows-1252 among UTF-8 ones.
A JSON array among NDJSON files, or an NDJSON file among JSON arrays.
A record missing its closing brace.
A number or boolean written as a string.
A file whose timestamp columns are stored at another unit than the rest.
A file whose timestamp columns are stored as INT96, as Hive and Impala wrote them.
A file whose decimal columns are stored one digit of scale wider than the rest.

ListedFault.description: A fault a fault list names: one `malformed_rows` writes, or one `cdc` places.

StreamFault.description: A fault `cdc` places in a change stream, listed in `_faults.jsonl` beside it.

oneOf.description: A change written a second time, after its key's last change.
A change written after its key's last change, in a later file than its commit time.
